primaryFocus.evidenceScope: Formula-first §9.5.2 hierarchy over above-tail ranks 1–11; D5 guard per §9.5.3.
primaryFocus.rationale: The D5 moisture guard clears its cluster-size criterion by exactly one member and then fails criterion 2, which forbids a rich R1/R4 architecture from being read as M5. This formula is a four-lipid butter/oil stack in ranks 4–7 whose three cluster members are the category's three cheapest and most universal humectants, one of them at tail_index − 1. Reading it as humectant-forward would be precisely the 'rich mask silently reading as moisture mask' that D5 and §6 rule 3 were written to prevent. No other route clears, so step 8 applies. E2 ceiling: an honest fallback, not a quality judgment.
evidenceSignals: GLYCERIN (rank 3) — near-universal category base ingredient; lexicon family 7 records it at rank 3–5 in every Balea/Gliss list checked and states its rank carries no moisture signal whatsoever
BETAINE (rank 9) — second cluster member
PANTHENOL (rank 11) — third cluster member, at tail_index − 1
BUTYROSPERMUM PARKII BUTTER (4), COCOS NUCIFERA OIL (5), GLYCINE SOJA OIL (6), PERSEA GRATISSIMA OIL (7) — the dominant M1 architecture the cluster would have to outweigh
no protein, no bond, no silicone, no above-tail polymer
claims: 'tiefenpflegend für Locken & trockenes Haar', 'mit Sheabutter, Kokosöl & Avocadoöl' — a richness story, not a hydration story
primaryFocus.derivation: Step 1 baseline exclusion applied. Step 2: the four lipids plus two cationics plus fatty alcohol are ONE M1 observation. Step 3: `repair` blocked (no route of any kind); `curl_support` REFUSED on the AP-03-CURLBAR ground (its test is met by nothing but the baseline, and the curl claim cannot create the route); `color_care` blocked; `lightness` blocked (weight `high`). Step 4: the D5 guard is applied — criterion 1 passes, criterion 2 FAILS. Step 5 `shine` blocked (§9.5.4 criterion 1: no alignment-oriented route, and two R4b heavy lipids sit above the tail). Step 6 `smoothing` rejected. Step 7 `detangling` rejected. Step 8 → `general`.
thresholdReasoning: Clears `general`: §9.5.2 step 8 — a capable conventional mask where no differentiator clears threshold.

`moisture` is the closest competitor and is REFUSED at D5 guard criterion 2, not at criterion 1. Criterion 1 passes: Glycerin @3, Betaine @9 and Panthenol @11 are three distinct R9-list humectants above the tail with two non-glycerin. Criterion 2 — 'Not the baseline. Intensive conditioning alone never qualifies. A rich R1/R4 architecture is M1, not M5' — fails: the material direction of this formula is a contiguous four-lipid block including two R4b heavy lipids at ranks 4 and 5, and the three cluster members are exactly the humectants lexicon family 7 identifies as category-universal and signal-free. §5 R9's stated purpose is that hydrolyzed proteins, fatty alcohols, esters and oils are kept out of the cluster precisely so 'rich mask' cannot read as 'moisture mask'; awarding moisture here would defeat that separation by the back door.
`curl_support` does not apply: refused on the same ground as its near-twin #03 (AP-03-CURLBAR). Consistency between the twins was treated as a requirement, not a coincidence.

`smoothing` does not apply: the substantial-lipid conjunct of step 6 is met, but dry surface control is not the clearest practical differentiator in a formula with no silicone, no above-tail polymer and no film former — the credited route is softening.
`detangling` does not apply: slip is category baseline (step 7's stated expectation).
`shine` does not apply: criterion 1 fails on both halves — no alignment-oriented R2/R3 route above the tail, and a comparatively HIGH lipid load.
counterSignals: Criterion 2 has no operational test anywhere in the standard, so this refusal is a reasoned reviewer judgment rather than a mechanical result. A blind reviewer running criterion 1 alone would return `moisture`, and would not be misapplying any written threshold. This is the cohort's most likely single point of blind-lane disagreement after AP-08-TIEBREAK. See AP-10-CRITERION2.
Confidence is held at `moderate` for exactly that reason.
limitations: `general` is a statement about evidence, not about product quality — this is a well-built rich curl mask.

Consistency note: #03 and #10 receive identical nine-field profiles. That is the intended outcome for architecturally equivalent formulas, and it was achieved here only because criterion 2 absorbed a tail-marker difference that criterion 1 would have let through.

adjudicationPoints.title: D5 guard criterion 2 is the standard's loosest binding gate, and it decides this product alone
adjudicationPoints.body: §9.5.3 criterion 1 is fully operational (≥3 distinct humectants above the tail, ≥2 non-glycerin). Criterion 2 is a sentence: 'Not the baseline. Intensive conditioning alone never qualifies. A rich R1/R4 architecture is M1, not M5.' It has no threshold, no count, and no comparison. On this product criterion 1 passes by one member and criterion 2 is the only thing standing between a butter-heavy curl mask and a `moisture` headline. I refused moisture, on the reasoning that the cluster is the category's three cheapest humectants against a contiguous four-lipid block including two R4b heavies at ranks 4 and 5, and that §5 R9 exists precisely to stop rich masks reading as moisture masks. A blind reviewer running criterion 1 mechanically returns `moisture` and violates no written rule. Candidate fixes, none adopted here: (i) require the cluster to be positionally competitive — e.g. at least two members ranked above the highest-ranked R4b lipid; (ii) disqualify `moisture` outright when two or more R4b heavy lipids are above the tail, mirroring §9.5.4's low-lipid-load criterion for shine; (iii) require at least one cluster member that is not glycerin, betaine or panthenol, since lexicon family 7 marks those as category-universal. Note that fix (ii) has an attractive symmetry: shine already requires a low lipid load, and moisture arguably should too. Also note the interaction with AP-03-TWINS — under criterion 1 alone, the two Bali Curls twins split onto different primary focuses purely because their tail markers differ by two ranks.

adjudicationPoints.title: Glycerin at rank 3 counts as a full cluster member despite the lexicon calling it signal-free
adjudicationPoints.body: Lexicon family 7 states that glycerin sits at rank 3–5 in every German-market list checked, is 'a base ingredient of the category, present regardless of positioning', and that 'its rank carries no moisture signal whatsoever'. §9.5.3 criterion 1 nonetheless counts it as one of the three required members, requiring only that two others be non-glycerin. On a three-member cluster that means one third of the qualifying evidence is an ingredient the lexicon says carries no signal. This did not change the outcome here (criterion 2 refused the value anyway) but it would on any formula with glycerin plus two other cheap members and a leaner lipid load. Candidate fix: exclude glycerin from the count entirely and require three non-glycerin members — which is arguably what D5's ruled sentence 'at least two FURTHER distinct humectants' plus 'glycerin alone never qualifies' already means.

assumptionNotes: Reviewer policy applied to every record in this lane: §3.1's hard cut determines above-tail membership without exception; the lexicon §0.2 boundary-band caution is applied only as a confidence modifier and never moves a value. Note that Panthenol @11 sits at tail_index − 1 and was therefore counted in full toward the cluster under this policy — the refusal of `moisture` rests on criterion 2, not on the band.
